title: Model second opinion (E4): a second, already-preloaded model's own answer to a run's delivered messages, compared against the run's already-recorded evidence
description: clozn.runs.second_opinion.build_second_opinion's output. `arm_a` (the ANCHOR) is built entirely from the original run's own already-persisted evidence -- it never calls a worker, so it is always available even when the original model is no longer loaded, and it is never replaced or outvoted by `arm_b`. `arm_b` (the SECOND OPINION) is one fresh completion from a different, already-preloaded model given the SAME delivered messages. The two arms are independently typed and independently statused ON PURPOSE: there is no top-level success/failure flag anywhere in this document, because one arm's failure must never invalidate the other's evidence (owner's spec, verbatim). `comparison` is present only when BOTH arms produced comparable natural-language text; every other field it would need is honestly omitted rather than null-padded when the two arms are not directly comparable (different templates, a tool/schema contract, missing text). This document NEVER carries a per-token probability or logprob from either model -- two models' logprobs are not on a shared scale, so this schema has no field for one at all (see the module docstring for why).

worker_identity.description: Identifying facts about the exact worker behind one arm. Every key OMITTED, never null-padded, when it could not be honestly determined for that arm.

arm_a.description: The anchor arm: the run's own already-recorded answer and identity, read verbatim -- no live call, no re-verification, no re-generation. `status` mirrors clozn.answer-claims.v1's own segmentation-state vocabulary (ok/empty/redacted/unavailable) rather than inventing a new one for the same underlying fact.

arm_b.description: The second-opinion arm: one fresh completion from a DIFFERENT already-preloaded model. `status` is independent of arm_a's -- a `refused` or `generation_error` here never removes arm_a from the document, and never becomes a top-level HTTP failure by itself (see the route docstring for the exact boundary between a pre-flight refusal and a recorded generation_error).

context_limit_compat.description: arm_a_prompt_tokens_estimate is measured under the ANCHOR model's own tokenizer, not arm_b's -- different tokenizers segment identical text into different counts, so this is always an ESTIMATE, never an exact fit/no-fit proof for arm_b. Never used to block a generation attempt; recorded as evidence only.

qualified_evidence_compat.description: Permanently 'anchor_only' for this schema version: v1 never computes claim-level support (E2) for the second-opinion arm, because that arm is deliberately never persisted as a run and E2's span addressing requires a real run id. Not a per-request failure -- a structural fact about this milestone, recorded so it is never mistaken for a silently-skipped measurement.

delivered_input.description: What was actually sent to arm_b: the SAME sanitized message list arm_a's own recorded `messages` was built from. `identical_across_arms` is always true in v1 -- this implementation never varies the delivered messages per arm -- but stays an explicit, checkable field rather than an assumed constant.

agreement.description: A LEXICAL proxy only -- word-type Jaccard DISTANCE between the two answers (0 = identical word-type sets, 100 = completely disjoint), the exact number clozn's corrective-retry compare view already surfaces. Never a semantic, entailment, or truth-preserving judgment, and never derived from any per-token probability of either model.

comparison.description: Present only when both arms produced comparable, non-empty natural-language text. Claim-level disagreement and support comparison are deliberately NOT fields here in v1 -- see compatibility.qualified_evidence.
